definition: Recommending additional products to use together with a chosen item.
example: We cross-sell a belt that goes with the jacket.

definition: The average purchase amount per transaction.
example: We look at the store's average transaction value on a per-transaction basis.
note: Here it is the average per transaction. When tallied as the average per customer, the denominator is different.

definition: A temporary store that operates only for a set period.
example: We open a pop-up store to introduce new products.

definition: Inventory that remains unsold over a long period.
example: We decide how to deal with the deadstock.

definition: The budget available for additional purchases under the sales and inventory plan.
example: We check the OTB before placing additional buys.

definition: Lowering the current selling price.
example: We decide the end-of-season markdown range.

definition: The ratio of quantity sold to quantity received within a set period.
example: Of 100 units received, 60 sold, so the sell-through rate is 60%.
note: Here it is quantity sold ÷ quantity received × 100. Check each company's standard for period, returns, and additional inbound stock.

definition: The share of store visits that resulted in a purchase.
example: We check the store conversion rate by looking at visitor count alongside transaction count.

definition: Placing an additional order for a product already ordered.
example: We reorder colors that sell well.

definition: The reference quantity at which an additional order is placed once inventory reaches that level.
example: We set the reorder point taking lead time into account.

definition: Extra inventory held to prepare for demand increases or delayed inbound stock.
example: We keep safety stock in case of shipping delays.

definition: A document bundling production information such as measurements, materials, and construction.
example: We hand the latest tech pack to the factory.

definition: A drawing that represents a garment's shape and sewing construction in a flat view.
example: We also mark the back-panel seam lines on the flat sketch.

definition: A list of the materials and quantities needed to make a product.
example: We also include the zipper and labels in the BOM.

definition: A table organizing a product's measurement points and specifications.
example: We revise the sleeve length on the spec sheet.

definition: The defined location and reference for taking a measurement.
example: We mark the chest-circumference POM on the flat sketch.

definition: Materials used besides the main fabric, such as buttons, zippers, and labels.
example: We match the trim colors to the fabric.

definition: The allowed range of deviation from the specification.
example: We set the overall-length tolerance at 0.5 cm.

definition: The margin left between the cutting line and the stitching line for sewing.
example: We note the seam allowance width on the flat sketch.
note: "Nuishiro" is a term found in older sewing terminology references.

definition: The task of putting a garment on to check fit, measurements, and silhouette.
example: After the sample fitting, we adjust the shoulder width.

definition: A test product used to check the worn state and measurements.
example: We check the sleeve movement with the fit sample.

definition: Notes written after a fitting on what to fix and where.
example: We send the fit comments along with photos.

definition: Approving the standard after finishing the fit review.
example: After fit approval, we move to the next production stage.

definition: The color or color-combination options offered for the same design.
example: This style comes in three colorways.

definition: The full set of sizes in which a product is offered.
example: We set the size run from XS to XL.

definition: The task of developing a base pattern into other sizes according to set rules.
example: We grade from the base M size.

definition: A large bundle of work that can be broken into several smaller tasks or stories.
example: We group the sign-up improvements into an epic.

definition: A description of a desired feature and its reason from the user's perspective.
example: We write down why the user needs it in the user story.

definition: A higher-level undertaking that groups several epics under a common goal.
example: We drive an initiative to improve the search experience.

definition: The shared criteria by which a team recognizes work as done.
example: We include testing and documentation updates in the DoD.

definition: The conditions for judging that a particular requirement has been met.
example: We also note handling of empty input in the acceptance criteria.

definition: The future burden on improvements caused by choices in structure or implementation.
example: We clean up the technical debt from accumulated duplicate logic.

definition: The work of improving code structure while keeping external behavior unchanged.
example: We refactor while leaving the functionality as is.

definition: The role that manages the backlog and priorities to maximize product value.
example: We set the next sprint's priorities with the PO.
note: The purchase order in fashion and retail and the Product Owner in development and product teams have different meanings.

definition: The role that helps the team understand Scrum and work effectively.
example: The Scrum Master helps resolve collaboration blockers.

definition: A practice of frequently merging changed code and automatically building and verifying it.
example: We run CI tests on every PR.

definition: The process of producing a runnable or deployable artifact from source.
example: We check why the build failed.

definition: The process in which another developer reads and reviews the changed code.
example: We get a code review before merging.

definition: A practice of keeping verified changes ready to be deployed at any time.
example: We put an approval step in the continuous delivery pipeline.
note: CD stands for both Continuous Delivery and Continuous Deployment, so check whether it includes automatic reflection to production.

definition: A practice of automatically reflecting verified changes all the way to the production environment.
example: Once all checks pass, we reflect changes via continuous deployment.
note: The timing of deployment and of releasing a feature to users can differ through mechanisms such as feature flags.

definition: The task of reflecting changed software into a running environment.
example: We deploy today's fixes to the production environment.

definition: The running environment that serves actual users.
example: We verify before reflecting changes to the production environment.

definition: A fix that resolves an urgent problem in a version currently in operation.
example: We handle the login failure with a hotfix.

definition: Putting out a software version so it can be used.
example: We include the improved features in this release.

definition: A test that connects and verifies the user's entire flow.
example: We run an E2E test from login through ordering.

definition: A test that quickly checks whether core features basically work.
example: We start with a smoke test after deployment.

definition: A test that checks whether the product satisfies business requirements.
example: The responsible person runs an acceptance test using real work scenarios.

definition: A test that checks system performance such as speed and stability.
example: We run a performance test for times with many concurrent users.

definition: A test in which a person operates it directly and checks the results.
example: We also review the screen flow with manual testing.

definition: A test that runs the verification process via scripts or tools.
example: We run repetitive checks as automated tests.

definition: A unit of software divided to take on an independent role. In front-end work it mainly means a reusable UI implementation unit that bundles screen structure and behavior.
example: We make the button component render in a disabled state based on the properties it receives.
note: This explanation centers on UI components. The reusable source in a design tool and the actual implementation code are distinguished.

definition: A master unit of UI design made for repeated use, such as buttons and input fields. Its presentation is managed consistently across screens through instances and variants.
example: After editing the master button component, we also check the linked instances.
note: This is the design-tool context of a component. We define its correspondence with the component in implementation code and hand it to the development team.

definition: Variations of the same component such as size and state.
example: We map the design's disabled variant to the disabled property and style.
note: Here it means a variation of a UI component.

definition: Variations of the same component such as size and state.
example: We add a disabled variant of the button.
note: Here it means a variation of a UI component.

definition: A collection that bundles related variants together.
example: Looking at the component set we received, we implement the button's size and state combinations.

definition: A collection that bundles related variants together.
example: We bundle the button variants into a component set.

definition: A shared, named unit for design values such as color and spacing.
example: We link color design tokens to CSS variables to reflect theme changes.

definition: A shared, named unit for design values such as color and spacing.
example: We manage the accent color as a design token.

definition: A presentation system of colors, styles, and so on applied to the same UI.
example: We save the user's theme setting and apply it on their next visit as well.

definition: A presentation system of colors, styles, and so on applied to the same UI.
example: We prepare a light theme and a dark theme.

definition: The process of passing the design information and intent needed for implementation to the development team.
example: At handoff we check the loading and error states and keyboard behavior before implementing.
note: It includes not only passing files but also explaining states, behaviors, and edge conditions.

definition: The process of passing the design information and intent needed for implementation to the development team.
example: At handoff we also explain the behavior for each state.
note: It includes not only passing files but also explaining states, behaviors, and edge conditions.

definition: A system of shared rules and reusable elements for building a consistent product.
example: We pull the button component from the design system and wire it into the checkout screen.

definition: A system of shared rules and reusable elements for building a consistent product.
example: We build new screens following the design system too.

definition: The image area extended beyond the finished line to allow for cutting error.
example: Please fill the background color all the way to the bleed.

definition: Marks that indicate where to cut printed material.
example: We add trim marks to the output file.

definition: Marks for aligning the color plates so they print in the same position.
example: We use the registration marks to check for plate misalignment.
note: On the print floor they are also called "donbo."

definition: An arrangement of color patches used to check print color and density.
example: We check the print quality by looking at the color bar.

definition: A method of printing a specified color with a separate ink, or that color itself.
example: We discuss printing the brand color as a spot color.

definition: A color system for specifying and communicating colors by number and so on.
example: We check the Pantone number together with the physical chip.
note: Depending on the material, printing method, and whether it is coated, the same number can appear as a different color.

definition: Checking color and production quality at the printing site.
example: We do a press check during the first print run.

definition: Related merchandise made based on a brand or content.
example: We design goods based on the album concept.

definition: Confirming something that has been discussed.
example: We fix the meeting date for Friday.
note: Here it means finalizing a schedule or plan. In development, fixing a bug means correcting an error.

definition: Developing an idea or plan into something more concrete.
example: We develop the chosen direction a bit further.

definition: A roughly outlined state before the details are refined.
example: Let's first share a rough direction.
note: This is framed as describing an early state with details omitted, rather than a judgment of low quality.

definition: An opinion delivered after reviewing work.
example: We gather the feedback and deliver it all at once.

definition: The due date by which work must be finished.
example: The deadline for this task is Thursday.

definition: The key measurement metric for judging the degree of goal achievement.
example: We agree on KPIs aligned with the team's goals.
note: To compare, you must define not only the metric name but also the formula, period, data source, and target value.

definition: A method of representing color with red, green, and blue light.
example: We check images for screen use against the RGB standard.

definition: A method of representing color with red, green, and blue light.
example: We check images for screen use against the RGB standard.

definition: A method of representing color with red, green, and blue light.
example: We check the color of product photos for our own online store on an RGB screen.

definition: A method of representing color with cyan, magenta, yellow, and black inks.
example: For print files we check the result of the CMYK conversion.

definition: A method of representing color with cyan, magenta, yellow, and black inks.
example: For print files we check the result of the CMYK conversion.

definition: A method of representing color with cyan, magenta, yellow, and black inks.
example: Before printing the lookbook, we check with a CMYK conversion whether the garment colors shift.

definition: A setting that prints over the top without knocking out the color plate beneath.
example: We check the overprint on the black text.

definition: A treatment that removes the underlying color where the top object will print.
example: We check whether the overlapping area is set to knockout.

definition: A feature that adjusts the arrangement and size of elements according to content and rules.
example: Even as the text grows, Auto Layout keeps the spacing.

definition: A feature that adjusts the arrangement and size of elements according to content and rules.
example: We check the mockup's Auto Layout spacing and line-break rules and implement them in CSS.
note: This is a collaboration context of receiving Figma design values and implementing them. On the web, it is implemented with that environment's layout rules such as CSS.

definition: The margin between a container's edge and the content inside it.
example: We increase the left and right padding of the button.

definition: In the CSS box model, the inner spacing placed between the content area and the border.
example: We add left and right padding to the button and check that the content isn't cut off even with long text.

definition: The spacing between elements placed side by side.
example: We unify the gap between cards.

definition: The spacing placed between rows or columns in CSS Grid, Flexbox, and the like. It is distinct from the container's outer margin and each item's inner padding.
example: We set the card list's gap to 16px and also check the vertical spacing after wrapping.

definition: A setting that sizes an element to wrap its inner content.
example: We set the label frame to hug.
note: This describes a sizing setting in Figma's Auto Layout.

definition: A setting that sizes an element to wrap its inner content.
example: We make a label set to hug in the mockup grow with the text length in code too.
note: This is Figma's fit-to-content sizing setting. Since it is not a CSS property name, we implement it while also checking the content, minimum size, and wrapping conditions.

definition: A setting that fills the available space of the parent container.
example: We set the input field's width to fill container.
note: This is a sizing setting in Figma's Auto Layout. Its scope depends on the parent frame's settings.

definition: A setting that fills the available space of the parent container.
example: We implement an input field set to fill container so it fills the remaining width of the parent area.
note: This is Figma's fill-the-parent sizing setting. We check the parent's size and margins and translate it into web layout constraints.

definition: The activities and systems for managing relationships using customer information and contact history.
example: We link purchase history to the CRM.

definition: The activities and systems for managing relationships using customer information and contact history.
example: We segment CRM message targets using purchased apparel items and size history.

definition: The activities and systems for managing relationships using customer information and contact history.
example: We pass the order-completed event and customer identifier to the CRM integration API.

definition: Improving a site so that search engines understand and find its content.
example: We review the SEO of product descriptions and titles.

definition: Improving a site so that search engines understand and find its content.
example: We review the title and description of a coat product on our own store from an SEO perspective.

definition: Improving a site so that search engines understand and find its content.
example: We review the HTML and meta information against SEO standards so search engines can read the content.

definition: Visits that come from natural search rather than paid search ads.
example: We also watch changes in organic traffic.
note: Here it means natural search traffic. Some teams also call all traffic obtained without paid spend "organic."

definition: Visits that come from natural search rather than paid search ads.
example: We look at the organic traffic to our store from natural searches related to linen shirts.
note: Here it means natural search traffic. Some teams also call all traffic obtained without paid spend "organic."

definition: Values appended to a URL to distinguish traffic source and campaign.
example: We distinguish the UTM for each banner link.
note: In Google's documentation it distinguishes source, medium, campaign, and so on. Do not put personally identifiable information in the URL values.

definition: Values appended to a URL to distinguish traffic source and campaign.
example: We split the UTM of the lookbook link and the influencer styling link to compare traffic.
note: In Google's documentation it distinguishes source, medium, campaign, and so on. Do not put personally identifiable information in the URL values.

definition: Values appended to a URL to distinguish traffic source and campaign.
example: We test whether the UTM parameters are preserved even after a redirect.
note: In Google's documentation it distinguishes source, medium, campaign, and so on. Do not put personally identifiable information in the URL values.

definition: The cost of one ad click.
example: We check the CPC of the new-product ad.

definition: The cost of showing an ad 1,000 times.
example: We compare the CPM of the collection ads.

definition: The ratio of clicks to ad impressions.
example: We compare the CTR by product image.
note: It is calculated as clicks ÷ impressions × 100. Distinguish it from metrics that use the number of people as the denominator.

definition: The ratio of revenue generated relative to ad spend.
example: We check the ROAS of the new-product ad on our own store.
note: It is a revenue-based metric. It does not directly mean profit margin or net profit.

definition: The ratio of visits or clicks that led to a target action.
example: We review the CVR after improving the detail page.
note: You must also check whether the denominator is clicks or visits and which action is defined as a conversion.

definition: The cost per one target action such as a purchase or sign-up.
example: We adjust the budget based on the first-purchase CPA.

definition: The total number of times an ad was displayed.
example: We check the impressions of the seasonal campaign.

definition: The number of people reached by an ad, excluding duplicates.
example: We check the reach of the collection ad.

definition: Deciding the audience to whom an ad will be shown.
example: We target it to fit new customers.

definition: The people an ad or content is aimed at.
example: We split out the audience of recently purchasing customers.

definition: A group of customers divided by shared characteristics.
example: We create segments by purchase cycle.

definition: A method of advertising again to people who had prior contact, such as a visit.
example: We retarget customers who abandoned their cart.

definition: A page people arrive at by clicking an ad, email, and so on, designed to drive a specific action.
example: We build a landing page for the seasonal promotion.
